# PEN-3259 — the login veto read the whole pod transcript, not the result event

**Vendored files changed:** `src/server/parse.ts`, `src/server/parse.test.ts`

**Issue:** [PEN-3259](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-3259) · **PR:** [#1868](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/1868)

Stopped `isClaudeTransientUpstreamError`'s LOGIN VETO reading the whole pod transcript. The mirror image of PEN-3223 (the last row in the now-frozen `PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md`): that change narrowed the *granting* haystack, and explicitly left the veto wide on the argument that a veto can only ever SUPPRESS the transient label, so narrowing it would *widen* what the function grants. That argument is sound about direction and silent about cost, and the cost is what this measures. `detectClaudeLoginRequired` joins `parsed.result` + `parsed.errors[]` + `stdout` + `stderr`, and `stdout` is the entire pod log — so a run that merely *mentions* auth vetoes its own true capacity refusal. Measured over 446 failed runs carrying a terminal result event (retained logs from 2026-09-12; 403 x281, 429 x95, 503 x70): the transcript-reading veto fires **91** times, the bounded-surface veto **0**. Not one run in the corpus reports an auth failure on its own result event, so every firing was transcript-only, and 89 of the 91 are the bare word `unauthorized` — which an agent reading a 401 handler, or this very issue's text, writes into its own transcript. What the narrowing admits is enumerated rather than counted: 27 runs move from no retry family at all to `transient_upstream` — 19 Penstock capacity refusals, each carrying an explicit reset timestamp, and 8 Anthropic 503s. **No 403 is admitted and no run loses a transient label.** `detectClaudeLoginRequired` itself is UNCHANGED, deliberately: it is shared, and `stdout` is the right surface for its other callers, which ask whether a run needs re-authentication before any result event exists. What changed is what this one rule passes it, gated on the terminal result event so the no-result-event path keeps the transcript read — that is where a login prompt actually appears. The `claude-local` twin gets the same change and is the MORE exposed copy: over the same 446 transcripts its regex fires 308 times against this copy's 91, with `failed to authenticate` — ordinary git/gh/ssh/registry output — accounting for 285 on its own. 

**Stacking order is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** On the pre-PEN-3223 wide haystack this narrowing *alone* takes the transient label from 237 runs to 301 and the 403s inside it from 99 to 136, i.e. it makes that defect worse; with PEN-3223 in front of it the 403s go to 0. Do not cherry-pick this ahead of PEN-3223. Recorded as a per-change entry rather than an integrity-hash recompute: this branch was restacked onto PEN-3223's linearized head after BLO-35109 withdrew the stored hash, so the hash regeneration its commit message originally described no longer exists to perform. 

**Ally review follow-up (head `9d6a6296`), and it found the PEN-3223 defect reintroduced in the sibling veto.** The new login veto gated on `parsed` TRUTHINESS while the haystack 20 lines below gated on `isClaudeTerminalResultEvent(parsed)` — so the comment added in the same change, claiming the veto reads its surfaces "under the same `parsed` condition" as the haystack, was factually untrue, and the two conditions differed on exactly the population the shape gate was introduced to protect. In THIS copy that is inert for the reason recorded in PEN-3223's PROVENANCE-CHANGES.md row (`parsed` is `resultJson` with `scanForResultEvent` recovery, both hard-checking `type === "result"`, so a truthy non-result object cannot arrive); in the `claude-local` twin it is live, and the failure is a fail-OPEN: a run with a truthy non-result `parsed` and a CLI login prompt reaching only `stdout` gets handed `stdout: ""`, sees nothing on `result`/`errors[]`/`stderr` (all empty for that shape), and the wide haystack — correctly selected, since this is not a result event — then matches any transient token in the transcript and retries an auth failure as `claude_transient_upstream`. Both gates now test the shape in both copies. The twin's truthy-non-result test is added **here** as well, where it is unreachable: writing the gate on the shape in both copies is pointless if only one copy is pinned, and twin drift is what produced this finding and two before it. 

**The second Critical is the one worth carrying forward, because it generalises past this change: a narrowing applied only inside the classifier was a no-op at every production call site.** `claude-local`'s `execute.ts` computes `detectClaudeLoginRequired` over the full `proc.stdout` and consumes `requiresLogin` BEFORE the narrowed classifier is reached (`:1218`, consumed at `:1257`/`:1266`/`:1283` on the `!parsed` path and `:1406`-`:1450` on the parsed one), so a transcript-only auth token suppressed the real verdict upstream of the fix and CI stayed green on classifier-level tests that never composed the decision the way production makes it. That call site is now narrowed on the same shape gate, and an execute-level composition test was added — a mirror, not the real function, since this adapter exports no `classifyClaudeUpstreamFailure` to drive, so it must be kept in step with that call site. 

**One hazard in the recommended remedy was measured rather than adopted as written:** narrowing `execute.ts:1193` wholesale, as the review phrased it, would also have dropped the operator-facing login URL, because `detectClaudeLoginRequired` derives `loginUrl` from `[stdout, stderr]` **independently** of `requiresLogin` (`parse.ts:193`) — a second regression in a field the review did not mention. Only the CLASSIFICATION input is narrowed; `loginMeta.loginUrl` keeps the whole transcript. Both new tests are positive-controlled rather than asserted: reverting the gate alone turns the truthy-non-result test red and nothing else, and widening the composition helper back to the full transcript turns that block red — a test that cannot fail on the defect it names is the thing this PR has now been caught by twice. 

**What narrowing the `execute.ts` gate admits is enumerated structurally, and the enumeration closes without a second corpus run, because every consumer is bounded by reading the source rather than the logs.** `requiresLogin` gates five things there. (1) `transientUpstream` — the intended family, already measured at the classifier in this entry. (2) `quotaExhausted` — newly reachable, and it reads `isClaudeQuotaExhausted(parsed)`, i.e. the terminal result event ONLY, with no `stdout` parameter at all, so it cannot be transcript-poisoned in either direction. (3) `providerQuota` — narrowed too, in a follow-up round (Ally review `5407967369` at `bcd15e25`). As first written this item said the quota rule was left wide and so "stays exactly as suppressed as before"; that was true of the gate on its own and wrong about the composition. `isClaudeProviderQuotaError` vetoes on `detectClaudeLoginRequired` internally, so on the whole transcript it stayed suppressed while (1) no longer was, and a terminal result matching `CLAUDE_PROVIDER_QUOTA_RE` but not `CLAUDE_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED_RE` (`ServiceQuotaExceededException` is in both the quota and the transient regex, so it needs no co-occurring token) whose transcript mentioned auth was not left unfamilied: the next rule claimed it as `claude_transient_upstream`, the schedule the quota-first ordering exists to avoid. `execute.ts` now hands `isClaudeProviderQuotaError` the same narrowed `stdout` (`isClaudeTerminalResultEvent(parsed) ? "" : proc.stdout`), and hands it to `isClaudeTransientUpstreamError` as well, because that rule's internal quota suppression also reads `stdout` and must agree with the narrowed quota gate — left wide, a quota token present only in the tool output vetoes a genuine 429's transient verdict while the narrowed gate says "not quota", and the run drops to no family. Two populations move, on the parsed result-event path only (`!parsed` and truthy-non-result inputs are byte-identical, since the shape gate is false there). **P1** — quota token in the result, auth token only in the transcript: `claude_auth_required` on master, `claude_transient_upstream` before this round, `provider_quota` now. **P2** — quota token only in the transcript, none in the result: `provider_quota` on master and before this round, a label taken from transcript content, which is the class this entry removes; now whatever the result event supports — `claude_transient_upstream` for a 429, otherwise no family. Both are pinned against the real `execute()` in `execute.login-veto-routing.test.ts`. Neither population is covered by the corpus run below, which predates this round: P1 and P2 are enumerated from the source, not measured. (4)/(5) `claudeReportedSuccess`, `failed` and `resolvedErrorCode`, and this is the one worth stating plainly because it is a defect nobody had named: `failed` ORs in `parsedIsError` and `requiresLogin`, so under the wide read a run whose terminal event reported **clean success** was marked failed and coded `claude_auth_required` purely because its transcript somewhere contained an auth-shaped token — in this copy, `failed to authenticate`, which is ordinary git / gh / ssh / registry output. The narrowing removes exactly those false positives and nothing else, and critically it does **not** weaken the override those lines exist for: the motivating case recorded in the comment above them is `{subtype:"success", is_error:false, result:"Not logged in · Please run /login"}` — an envelope that lies while `parsed.result` tells the truth — and `result` is a bounded surface the narrowed read still consults. So the behaviour that block was written to protect is preserved by construction, while the transcript false-positive class it accidentally also caught is dropped. That asymmetry is why this gate could be narrowed safely; (3) records why `isClaudeProviderQuotaError`'s then had to follow it. **The enumeration above was then checked against logs rather than left as a source argument, on a fresh corpus — 114,342 retained run logs (2026-09-12 onward, re-scanned 2026-10-01), of which 408 carry a terminal `result` event and were evaluated through a harness mirroring `execute.ts:1235` and every consumer at `:1423-1467`.** The login veto fires **94** times on the wide transcript against **18** on the bounded surfaces, so 76 of 94 firings are transcript-only. Among the 122 runs whose result event is `is_error: true`, **17 verdicts change and all 17 move in the intended direction**: 14 × `429` `claude_auth_required` → `claude_transient_upstream` (Penstock capacity refusals recovering the retry family this entry exists to restore) and 3 × `400` `claude_auth_required` → no family, which is correct — those are BYOS allocation errors (`Allocations exist for org … but none is current`), permanently unretryable, and the auth label was simply wrong. **Regressions: 0.** Nothing loses a non-auth label, and **no 403 is admitted** — 18 are present in the corpus and not one changes verdict, which is the PEN-3223-inherited safety property holding on new data. The fourth consumer's defect is confirmed empirically as well as structurally: **59 runs whose terminal result event reported CLEAN SUCCESS had the wide veto fire and the bounded veto not fire**, i.e. they were marked `failed` and coded `claude_auth_required` on transcript content alone. Two honesty caveats on that 59, neither of which touches the 17-verdict result above. First, these are k8s pod logs with the `claude-local` regex evaluated over them, so like the 308-vs-91 comparison earlier in this entry it is an exposure measurement against representative agent output, not a claim about runs this adapter served. Second, the 408 were pre-filtered by grepping for the literal `"is_error":true` anywhere in the file, which deliberately over-selects transcripts containing error-shaped JSON — so 59/286 is a rate *within a biased slice* and must not be read as a fleet rate. What the slice establishes is that the class is real and large, not how common it is.

**Comment-only round (head `de18b8ce`, Ally review `5419338840`: 0 Critical, 0 Important, 3 suggestions).** No runtime change — `git diff` on this round touches comments and this entry only, so every test and measurement above still describes the shipped behaviour. Two of the three suggestions were accepted as written and the third is deferred to a tracked row. (1) The `buildClaudeTerminalResultHaystack` docstring in the `claude-local` copy (`parse.ts:441`) still carried the pre-PEN-3223 rationale — *"the first two can only ever SUPPRESS a transient label … None of them grants a retry family off transcript text"* — and that is **false for `isClaudeProviderQuotaError`**, independent of this PR: it suppresses only in its one internal role inside `isClaudeTransientUpstreamError` (`:789`), while at its direct call sites it GRANTS `provider_quota` as both `errorCode` and `errorFamily` (`execute.ts:1293` → `:1327`/`:1331`; `:1457` → `:1511`/`:1517`). The stale text sat three hundred lines above the lines this PR narrowed and told a maintainer the wide builder was self-justifying, so it was an invitation to widen `:1459`/`:1472` back — the one thing the change cannot survive. It is corrected, and the same-input requirement is now recorded at `isClaudeProviderQuotaError`'s OWN definition (`:808`) rather than only in the sibling function that happens to call it, with both comments pointing at the pin in `execute.login-veto-routing.test.ts`. (2) The structural enumeration gained the one consumer it did not cover: classification is narrowed on the result-event path but the SCHEDULE is not — `extractClaudeRetryNotBefore` (`execute.ts:1477`) still reads the full `proc.stdout`, so a run whose family came from bounded surfaces can still draw its `retryNotBefore` from a transcript reset-shaped string that had no part in deciding it. Before this change the two agreed by construction. Left wide deliberately and **disclosed rather than bundled in**: the extractor prefers the structured `parsed` fields and only falls back to the haystack (`parse.ts:676-681`), and narrowing it changes the retry SCHEDULE, which the 114k-log run scored no evidence for — it measured verdicts, not timestamps. Believed rare, explicitly **not a measured zero**. (3) Deferred to **[PEN-3829](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-3829)**, with a pointer left at the ladder so it is discoverable in-code: `isClaudeModelNotFoundError` reads the full transcript and ranks ABOVE both newly-narrowed families in `resolvedErrorCode`, while `errorFamily` is computed independently and does not consult it — so a genuine 429 whose transcript merely mentions `model not found` can emerge with `errorCode: "model_not_found"` beside `errorFamily: "transient_upstream"`. Same defect class, sibling consumer, and not free to fix: `model_not_found` is a PERMANENT label, so narrowing it WIDENS what gets a retry family, and that direction needs its own corpus measurement rather than inheriting this one's.
